extracted.intended_audience: corporate SEC-reporting professionals, accountants, and legal advisors preparing SEC filings for acquisitions (Form 8-K, registration statements, Form 10-K/20-F)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on performing the SEC 'significance' (investment, income, asset) tests for acquisitions and dispositions under S-X rules, including what financial information to use, pro forma rules, intercompany eliminations, and special exceptions. Applies to determinations of whether audited historical financial statements of an acquired business must be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amounts must be determined under the same accounting standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The financial information (e.g. total assets, revenue, net income) for both the acquired business and the registrant used to determine significance must be determined using the same comprehensive basis of accounting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A registrant that files US GAAP financial statements (or is required to provide reconciliation to US GAAP) performs the significance tests using US GAAP (as applicable to PBEs) amounts for the acquired business. Similarly, a registrant filing under IFRS performs the tests using IFRS amounts. Example: when a domestic registrant acquires a foreign business, determine numerator and denominator under US GAAP for PBEs even if the acquiree does not prepare/reconcile to US GAAP. [S-X Rule 1-02(w)(1)]

rubrics_metrics.name: Private-company accounting alternatives generally not permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: The financial information of the acquired business used to perform the significance tests may not be prepared using private company accounting alternatives; such effects must be excluded (with one narrow exception).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an acquiree used private-company alternatives (e.g., goodwill amortization), the registrant must adjust the pre-acquisition financial statements to exclude those effects (e.g., add back amortization and consider retrospective impairment testing). [Regs Comm 03/2014]

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — risk-free rate under Topic 842 allowed for significance tests only
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC staff will allow a registrant to determine significance using an acquired business’s financial information that includes the effects of applying the 'risk-free rate' private company alternative in Topic 842.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exception applies only for performing the significance tests. If the tests indicate that audited historical financial statements of the acquired business are required, those financial statements must comply with US GAAP recognition and measurement principles applicable to a PBE. [Regs Comm 10/2020]

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrant may not alter acquired business financial statement amounts (except reversing private alternatives)
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant is not permitted to alter the amounts in the financial statements of an acquired business when determining significance, except for reversing the effects of a private company accounting alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, even if the registrant plans to dispose of certain acquiree assets after acquisition, it cannot exclude those assets from the acquiree’s total assets for the tests. If results appear anomalous in light of facts and circumstances, the registrant could request relief from the SEC staff to use impaired asset values, but cannot unilaterally adjust amounts. [Question 3.3.100]

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted use of previously filed pro forma information (conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant may use previously filed pro forma information to perform the significance tests for a probable or consummated acquisition (or completed disposition) only if certain historical audited statements and pro forma information were previously filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, the registrant may use previously filed pro forma if it previously filed audited Rule 3-05 or Rule 3-14 financial statements for an earlier acquired business and the pro forma financial information required by S-X Article 11 for that earlier acquisition. If the registrant elects to use pro forma information, it must use it for all three significance tests and continue to do so for all subsequent acquisitions/dispositions until the next Form 10-K or Form 20-F is filed. [S-X Rule 11-01(b)(3)(i)(B)]

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of pro forma financial information are limited
rubrics_metrics.description: Pro forma financial information used in the significance tests is limited to amounts that reflect the combination of the historical financial information of the registrant and the acquired business, and the transaction accounting adjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pro forma information used to determine significance may not give effect to autonomous entity adjustments, management’s adjustments, or other transactions (e.g., receipt/use of offering proceeds). Probable acquisitions are excluded from pro forma information used in the tests. [S-X Rule 11-01(b)(3)(i)(B), FRM 2020.6]

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro forma may include financing effects directly related to previous acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Pro forma financial information used in the significance tests includes amounts that reflect transaction accounting adjustments, which may include the effects of material financing transactions directly related to previous acquisition(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC staff has commented that pro forma amounts may give effect to increased interest costs resulting from financing of previous acquisitions. However, other pro forma effects (e.g., proceeds of an unrelated subsequent offering) are not included. [Question 3.3.120]

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot use pro forma that gives effect to probable or individually insignificant acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: S-X Rule 3-05 does not permit significance to be determined using pro forma financial information that gives effect to probable or individually insignificant acquisitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A registrant is required to use the financial statements in its most recent Form 10-K to determine significance unless the limited conditions for using previously filed pro forma (see above) are met. However, previously filed pro forma amounts reflecting significant acquisitions/dispositions completed since last fiscal year‑end may be used in limited circumstances. [S-X Rule 11-01(b)(3)(i)(B)]

rubrics_metrics.name: If previously filed pro forma lacks year-end balance sheet, prepare year-end pro forma balance sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: If previously filed pro forma information does not include a balance sheet as of the latest fiscal year-end, a registrant choosing to use the previously filed pro forma must prepare a pro forma balance sheet as of its most recently completed fiscal year-end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The registrant uses that (previously unfiled) year-end pro forma balance sheet in its significance tests and must use the pro forma income statement amounts for that same completed fiscal year. [FRM 2025.3]

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro forma use rules for shell companies (SPACs) — generally not permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, pro forma information cannot be used to determine significance for a subsequent acquisition by a shell company (e.g., a SPAC), because the acquiree may be deemed the registrant’s predecessor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a registrant that began the year as a shell acquires a predecessor and then makes another acquisition in the same year, the SEC staff has stated the significance of that subsequent acquisition should be determined using the shell company's prior-year financial statements (which do not include the predecessor). If that yields a requirement to file information the registrant believes immaterial, the registrant may consult the SEC staff and consider requesting relief under S-X Rule 3-13. [FRM 2025.9, Regs Comm 09/2019]

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests must be performed per S-X Rule 3-05 (no alternative tests)
rubrics_metrics.description: To achieve consistent application and fair treatment, the SEC does not accept alternative significance tests; the tests must be performed based on S-X Rule 3-05 and related rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a registrant believes tests specify periods beyond those necessary to inform investors, it may make a written request to the SEC staff (CF-OCA) to waive one or more years of financial statements. [FRM 2020.1]

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment test — numerator and denominator (AWMV) and substitute
rubrics_metrics.description: Investment test numerator: registrant’s and its other subsidiaries’ investments in, and advances to, the acquired business (US GAAP purchase price). Denominator: the aggregate worldwide market value (AWMV) of the registrant’s voting and non-voting common equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AWMV is calculated daily from the last five trading days of the most recently completed month ending prior to the earlier of (a) the date the registrant announces the acquisition, or (b) the date of the acquisition agreement. All publicly available shares worldwide are included. If there is no AWMV, use the registrant’s consolidated total assets for the most recently completed fiscal year. [See section 3.4 and S-X Rule 1-02(w)(1)]

rubrics_metrics.name: Income test — lower of pretax income component or revenue component (component definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Income test numerator: the lower of (a) the pretax income component or (b) the revenue component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pretax income component = absolute value of the registrant’s and its other subsidiaries’ equity in the tested subsidiary’s consolidated income or loss from continuing operations before income taxes (after intercompany eliminations) attributable to controlling interests for the most recently completed fiscal year. Revenue component = registrant’s and subsidiaries’ proportionate share of the tested subsidiary’s consolidated total revenues (after intercompany eliminations) for the most recently completed fiscal year. The lower of the two is used. The revenue component does not apply if the registrant or the acquired business do not have material revenue in each of the two most recently completed fiscal years. [See section 3.5]

rubrics_metrics.name: Asset test — numerator and denominator definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Asset test numerator: registrant’s and other subsidiaries’ proportionate share of total consolidated assets of the tested subsidiary (after intercompany eliminations) as of the end of the most recently completed fiscal year. Denominator: registrant’s and subsidiaries’ consolidated total assets (after intercompany eliminations) as of the end of the most recently completed fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the most recently completed fiscal year amounts. [See section 3.6]

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not round the results of significance tests
rubrics_metrics.description: The results of the significance tests should not be rounded; significance is evaluated on the exact computed percentage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the significance is greater than 20% by any amount (e.g., 20.1%), it is significant. If less than 20% by any amount (e.g., 19.9%), it is not significant. [FRM 2015.13]

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude the acquired business from the denominator
rubrics_metrics.description: When performing the significance tests, the denominator in each test excludes assets, income, or revenues of the acquired business from the registrant’s consolidated financial information as of the prior year-end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: for the asset test use registrant’s total assets before acquisition (exclude acquiree). Performing the denominator including the acquiree would understate significance. [FRM 2015.10 and Example 3.3.110]

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate intercompany transactions as if always consolidated
rubrics_metrics.description: Intercompany transactions between the registrant and the acquired business are eliminated when performing the significance tests, as if the acquired business had always been consolidated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminations can affect numerator, denominator, or both depending on nature of the transaction. Examples: exclude preferred-stock dividends received by the acquiree from registrant in pretax income and exclude the acquiree’s investment in registrant from acquiree’s total assets for the asset test; exclude intercompany profit from acquiree’s pretax income; exclude intercompany revenue from acquiree’s revenues; exclude carrying amount of intercompany inventory from registrant’s total assets. These eliminations are only for the tests; if acquisition is significant, filed historical financials of the acquiree are not adjusted to eliminate transactions with registrant. [S-X Rule 1-02(w), FRM 2015.11 and Examples 3.3.120–130]

rubrics_metrics.name: When pro forma is used, continue use for all subsequent tests until next annual report
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant chooses to determine significance of an acquisition (or disposition) using its pro forma financial information, it must use pro forma financial information when performing all three significance tests and continue to do so for all subsequent acquisitions and dispositions until the next annual report on Form 10-K or Form 20-F is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This continuity requirement applies even if some individual acquisitions were tested using historical financial statements earlier in the year—once pro forma is elected/used, it governs subsequent testing. [S-X Rule 11-01(b)(3)(i)(B)(2)]
